questions.q: Propan-1-ol is oxidised with PCC in dry CH₂Cl₂. The product is:
questions.explain: PCC is a mild Cr(VI) oxidant that stops a 1° alcohol at the aldehyde. Aqueous chromic acid reagents such as Jones reagent would give propanoic acid.

questions.q: Why does PCC in CH₂Cl₂ not over-oxidise the aldehyde to a carboxylic acid?
options: Over-oxidation goes through the aldehyde hydrate RCH(OH)₂, which cannot form without water
Pyridine reduces the acid back to the aldehyde
The aldehyde forms a stable complex with chloride
questions.explain: An aldehyde is oxidised further only via its hydrate. In anhydrous CH₂Cl₂ no hydrate forms, so the aldehyde survives; in DMF, by contrast, PCC can give acids.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes Collins reagent?
options: Pyridine + CrO₃ + HCl, the salt C₅H₅NH⁺CrO₃Cl⁻
CrO₃ in dilute H₂SO₄ and acetone
questions.explain: Collins and Sarett reagents share the neutral complex CrO₃·2py: Collins in CH₂Cl₂, Sarett in pyridine. Adding HCl gives PCC, and CrO₃/H₂SO₄/acetone is Jones reagent.

questions.q: Which alcohol is NOT oxidised by PCC in CH₂Cl₂?
questions.explain: A 3° alcohol can form a chromate ester but has no α-hydrogen to remove, so no C=O can form. Benzyl and allylic alcohols give aldehydes and cyclohexanol gives cyclohexanone.
